item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The HSC and specified executive officials are directed to coordinate policy and operate and staff an interagency forum; these are present internal-management assignments without a substantive legal consequence for regulated parties.","evidence":"The HSC Principals Committee (HSC/ PC) shall be the senior interagency forum under the HSC for homeland security issues."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The Assistant to the President controls when the committee meets and sets its agenda, which is internal executive housekeeping with no legal consequence beyond committee operations.","evidence":"The Assistant to the President for Homeland Security shall determine the agenda"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The responsible executive official must arrange preparation of meeting papers, an internal administrative task whose consequence occurs in committee preparation.","evidence":"shall ensure that all necessary papers are prepared."},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"Executive officials and the HSC/DC are assigned joint performance, policy-review, staffing, and meeting functions; all consequences concern internal interagency organization and deliberation.","evidence":"The HSC Deputies Committee (HSC/ DC) shall serve as the senior sub-Cabinet interagency forum"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The Chairman must set meeting agendas after internal consultation, an immediate assignment of administrative responsibility rather than a dictated legal outcome.","evidence":"the Chairman shall determine the agenda"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The Chairman must ensure preparation of internal meeting materials, with no change to legal rights, duties, or agency legal outcomes.","evidence":"shall ensure that necessary papers are prepared."},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The HSC/PCCs are assigned ongoing coordination of policy development and implementation among federal agencies, a discretionary interagency-management function.","evidence":"shall coordinate the development and implementation of homeland security policies"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The committees must coordinate policy with state and local government and serve as interagency coordination forums, without prescribing a legally consequential result.","evidence":"shall coordinate those policies with State and local government."},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The committees must provide internal policy analysis, respond to presidential decisions, and include specified agency representatives; these are advisory, coordination, and staffing duties.","evidence":"They shall provide policy analysis for consideration by the more senior committees"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"The directive presently establishes and staffs internal policy-coordination committees, an organizational action expressly covered as internal management rather than a substantive legal effect.","evidence":"Eleven HSC/PCCs are hereby established"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"Executive personnel receive administrative duties and discretionary authority over invitations, additional committees, working groups, and attendance; these govern internal organization and do not dictate an external legal consequence.","evidence":"may establish subordinate working groups to assist the PCC in the performance of its duties."}]}
